v2Note: v2, 2026-08-22 - the humanoid vocabulary was the wrong domain. The pilot partition drew from armament-primary.humanoid and produced Keen Sword, Fleet Sabre, Honed Falchion. The author did nothing wrong; the pool held nothing else. v1 applied one rule to both frames - use the real domain vocabulary - and got the plant frame exactly right (stalk, pith, cambium, radicle, stolon, haustorium) while reaching, for humanoids, into a historical European arms-and-armour glossary. A glossary of falchions can only produce falchions, and this is Plants vs Zombies: read DemonSpeciesCatalog and the humanoid arsenal is a traffic cone, a bucket, a newspaper, a screen door, a football helmet, a vaulting pole, a pool float. Gear here is found and strapped on, not forged. The fix: all 16 humanoid noun pools rewritten, standard.humanoid included, against the graveyard, garage, suburb, hardware store, sports field and roadworks; plus the 10 humanoid class-rung adjective pools that had gone medieval alongside them (cloth, leather, plate, scale, blade, launcher, focus, signet, torc, seal). weapon.humanoid.blunt and offhand.humanoid.bulwark were left alone - kinetic and functional words survive the test unchanged. Words that already fit stayed exactly where they were: cleaver, hatchet, sling, harness, strap, boot, clog, cap, hood, vest, and the frame display words the roles need (hand, waist, face, shoulder, horn, ring, bandolier). The plant pools were not touched - they were right the first time and they are the standard the humanoid side is now written to. No pool key was renamed or removed; conceptPools, themeAdjectivePools and uniqueSetSeedPools were not opened. Disjointness was re-verified over the whole file after the swap, not over the changed pools alone: exact duplicates on canonical ids and on surface forms, and the near-duplicate stem check. Who re-runs: any partition that already drew from a humanoid pool. On wave-0 timing that is the pilot and nothing else, which is the whole reason this was fixed at one partition rather than at thirty.

_meta.purpose: The vocabulary the ~92 name-authoring partitions draw from. naming.v1.json froze the grammar (three patterns, four connectives, the collision normalizer) and explicitly handed this file the word pools plus the entry shape the normalizer needs. This file populates them. Its job is not to supply every word an author could want — it is to make the corpus varied on purpose rather than varied by luck, by giving each name axis its own reserved vocabulary and making the axes provably disjoint.
_meta.consumedBy: 60 base-type partitions (nouns + their role's class-rung adjectives), 20 unique partitions and 5 set partitions (theme adjectives + concepts + seeds, plus read access to every noun pool), 3 charm partitions (same theme access, no theme exclusivity - see openAmbiguities), and the V1 validator, which resolves every authored `name` through these entries before running naming.v1.json §3's collision check.
_meta.relationshipToNamingV1: naming.v1.json owns the grammar and the id namespaces; this file owns nothing but words. Three safety nets run together and none substitutes for another: id-namespace disjointness (no two partitions share a prefix), pool disjointness (this file - no canonical id is reachable from two name axes), and collision normalization (the same idea spelled four legal ways still rejects).
_meta.immutability: FROZEN v2. After the freeze: no canonical id changes pool, no canonical id is deleted, and no surface form is repointed to a different canonical id. Adding a surface form to an existing entry is the only safe in-place edit, and only if the new form is not already claimed - see selfCheck.surfaceFormUniqueness. Anything else is v3. v1 was frozen and then revised once, before the fleet ran, for the reason set out in v2Note - that is the only edit this file has taken and the only kind it should ever take.

entryShape.shape: { canonicalId, surfaceForms: { noun?: [..], adjective?: [..], ofConcept?: [..] }, rungAffinity? }
entryShape.whyThisShape: naming.v1.json §3 step 3 resolves a surface token to a canonical id through that word's registered surface forms, and its worked example is exactly `ash` with {noun: 'Ash', adjective: 'Ashen'}. Both spellings must land on one id or 'Ashen Fang' and 'Ash Fang' stop colliding. Every entry here honours that object shape; each slot carries an array because most words have more than one form an author will actually type.
entryShape.canonicalIdRule: `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`, and always the bare lowercase root of the entry's own primary surface form. This is deliberate and load-bearing: naming.v1.json §3 step 3 says an UNREGISTERED token resolves to itself, lowercased. Because every canonical id here equals its own lowercased primary form, a registered word and an unregistered one resolve the same way, so a pool gap degrades gracefully instead of splitting one idea across two ids.
entryShape.surfaceFormRule: Every surface form is a single token - no spaces, no hyphens, no apostrophes. naming.v1.json §3 step 2 tokenizes on whitespace and punctuation, so a two-word pool entry would never resolve as a unit. A two-word Concept phrase ('of the Charnel Bloom') is the author combining two single-token pool words, not a single pool entry.
entryShape.resolutionOrder: 1. Try the whole lowercased token against the registered surface forms. 2. Only if that misses, attempt naming.v1.json's 'fusion' decomposition into exactly two known pool words. 3. Only if that misses too, resolve the token to itself. Whole-token-first is required, because uniqueSetSeedPools entries are atomic compounds ('Thistledown', 'Ashenreap') that would otherwise decompose into their halves and collide with ordinary compound names. A seed is one word and one idea, not two.
entryShape.rungAffinity: Present on noun entries only. Values are classes.v1.json's own weight tags: light, medium-light, medium, medium-heavy, heavy. It is a pull, not a rule - it exists so a band-B author reaches for `casque` and a band-A author reaches for `coif` without anyone writing that instruction down 60 times.
entryShape.bandHint: Band A leans light / medium-light / medium; band B leans medium / medium-heavy / heavy. `medium` sits in both on purpose: the jewel ladder has three rungs (light/medium/heavy per classes.v1.json), so its middle weight has to be reachable from either band or band A's jewel pools would run thin.

disjointness.claim: Every canonical id in this file appears in exactly one pool, and every surface form in this file maps to exactly one canonical id. Both are machine-checked at build time, not asserted.
disjointness.whatItBuysYou: The collision normalizer can only work if one idea has one id. If `ash` lived in two pools, or if 'Ashen' were registered under `ash` in one pool and `ashen` in another, two authors could legally produce the same idea under different ids and the corpus-wide comparison in naming.v1.json §3 step 6 would pass them both.
howItIsGuaranteed: 1. Single source. All 95 pools are generated from one table. Nothing is appended by hand downstream.
2. Exact-duplicate check. Every canonical id is inserted into one global map; a second insertion is a build failure, not a warning. Same for every surface form across every slot of every entry.

3. Near-duplicate check. Canonical ids are also compared after crude suffix stripping (-ed, -ing, -ous, -al, -y, -s, -en, -ies, -ied, -ly) and doubled-consonant collapse. Any two ids that stem-collide are a build failure too. This is the check that caught the real problems: `guard`/`guarding`, `root`/`rooted`, `swarm`/`swarming`, `knot`/`knotted`, `weighted`/`weighty` - pairs the exact check happily allows and a reader would read as the same word. 24 such pairs were found and resolved by renaming one side. v2's humanoid rewrite was put through the same check before it landed and introduced no new pair. It cost ten candidate words: `rivet`, `bolt` and `clamp` stem onto thorned-chassis's `riveted`, `bolted` and `clamped`; `jar` onto weapon.humanoid.blunt's `jarring`; `coil` and `gutter` onto weapon.plant.lash's `coiling` and ember-harvest's `guttering`; and `layered`, `meshed`, `crackling` and `pressurised` were already spent on plant rungs. Every one of the ten was caught by the machine check, not by reading.
4. Grammar check. Canonical ids must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$; surface forms must be single tokens; neither may be one of naming.v1.json's four closed connectives (of, the, a, and).
5. Floor check. Every pool must meet its per-type minimum (see perPoolMinimums) or the build fails.
disjointness.whatDisjointnessIsNot: It is not partition exclusivity. Two partitions may legally read the same pool - naming.v1.json splits every role-frame into band A and band B, and both bands share that role's nouns, exactly as intended. Disjointness is a property of the vocabulary across name AXES (noun vs class adjective vs theme adjective vs concept vs seed), which is what the normalizer sees. Two authors reaching into the same noun pool for different nouns is fine; the same idea arriving under two canonical ids is not.
deliberateNearMisses: `graft` is a noun (jewel-minor-a.plant), a class rung id in classes.v1.json, and half of core.v1.json's plant role display names (graft-1 / graft-2). It is also close to the rarity rung `Grafted`. All of these are correct and none of them collide: class ids and rarity rung names are labels, never tokens inside an authored `name`, so the normalizer never sees them.
`almanac` is a concept (sunwoven-almanac), a theme name, and the ordinal-100 rarity rung. Same reasoning.

`signet`, `torc` and `seal` are registered nouns AND class rung ids. Safe because canonicalId equals the bare word: whether a token arrives as a class word or a pool noun it lands on the same id either way.

nounPools.why: Two base-type partitions share each role-frame's nouns (band A and band B) and each authors ~12 identities, so ~24 names come out of one pool. 16 nouns crossed with the 12 adjectives of any one class rung is 192 legal compounds per rung - the pool is not the constraint on variety, the author's taste is.

classRungAdjectivePools.why: A base-type partition uses one ladder's rungs. 16 nouns x 12 adjectives per rung leaves an author authoring 12 identities using under 7% of its own combination space.

themeAdjectivePools.why: A theme is read by up to 4 unique partitions (one per rung band) plus a set partition plus charms. 12 adjectives x 12 concepts x 10 seeds is comfortably more surface than ~70 names need.

conceptPools.why: Concepts feed only the of-construct pattern, which is roughly a third of authored names. 12 is generous against that share and keeps every concept genuinely distinct rather than padded.

uniqueSetSeedPools.why: Seeds are the scarcest thing here on purpose. A unique should feel singular; handing an author 30 pre-made proper nouns would make uniques feel generated, which is the exact failure this registry exists to prevent. 10 per theme covers the ~15 uniques a partition authors as SEEDS for names, not as the names themselves - the author still combines, inflects, and chooses.

reservedOutOfPools.rule: These words are not pool entries. They resolve to themselves under naming.v1.json §3 step 3, which is correct and intended - registering them would claim a canonical id for a label that is not part of the flavour vocabulary.
reservedOutOfPools.classLadderWordsNote: classes.v1.json supplies these as the item's material/class word - 'Sturdy Bark Helm' in naming.v1.json's own worked example. Four class words (signet, torc, seal, graft) ARE registered as nouns because they are also the natural head-noun for their role; the canonicalId-equals-bare-word rule makes that safe.
reservedOutOfPools.rarityRungWordsNote: core.v1.json's rung display names. A rung name never appears inside an authored `name`, so these are reserved out to stop an author accidentally building a base-type name that reads as a rarity claim. `almanac` appears as a CONCEPT for the sunwoven-almanac theme, which is the theme's own word rather than the rung's - flagged in deliberateNearMisses.
reservedOutOfPools.roleIds: The 15 frame-neutral roleIds (armament-primary, core-guard, ...) are mechanical, never displayed, and never pool words. The frame display words (main-hand, crown, muzzle, ...) ARE pool words, registered in their own role's noun pool in singular form - plurals are forbidden by naming.v1.json, so core.v1.json's `hands`, `leaves`, `roots` and `shoulders` appear here as hand, leaf, root, shoulder.
reservedOutOfPools.atomFamilyIds: atom.* family ids are mechanical (definitions.md §1) and are not this file's vocabulary. Where an English word coincides with a family stem (keen, warded, padding), the pool word is the ordinary English word and carries no mechanical meaning.

poolAccess._readFirst: Which partition may draw from which pool. Reading a pool you were not granted is the one way a wave-1 agent can defeat this registry: the words are still disjoint, but the corpus stops being varied by construction.

baseTypePartition.nouns: nounPools['{roleId}.{frame}'] - shared with the other band of the same role-frame
baseTypePartition.adjectives: classRungAdjectivePools['{ladder}.{frame}.{rungId}'] for every ladder legal on this role (see roleToLadders below) - a partition may use any rung of its ladder, but should weight toward the rungs matching its band
baseTypePartition.mustNotUse: themeAdjectivePools, conceptPools, uniqueSetSeedPools. A base type has a class, not a theme; themes belong to uniques, sets and charms. This is the single most important access rule in the file - a base type wearing a theme word is how 60 partitions start sounding like 20.
baseTypePartition.patterns: compound (<Adjective> <Base>) is the default. of-construct is available but should stay rare on base types, since concepts are theme-owned and a base type has no theme.

mayUse: any nounPools entry (a unique still occupies a role, and should sound like it)
classRungAdjectivePools of the ladders legal on the role it occupies
uniquePartition.mustNotUse: another theme's adjective, concept or seed pool. Theme pools are exclusive by theme, not by partition - the four rung bands of one theme share that theme's three pools, and coordinate only through the corpus-wide normalizer.

setPartition.partitionKey: themeId - 5 partitions (thorned-chassis, verdant-graft, rusted-legion, frostbitten-vanguard, sunwoven-almanac)
setPartition.mayUse: identical to uniquePartition for its own theme. Member pieces are ordinary base types and take base-type access rules for their role.

charmPartition.mayUse: any theme's adjective / concept pools, plus any noun pool. Charms are partitioned by power axis, not by theme, so no theme can be given to them exclusively.
charmPartition.obligation: A charm agent records the themeId it drew from on each entry, so a reviewer can see the spread. With three agents free-ranging over 13 themes, the corpus-wide normalizer is the only automatic protection - see openAmbiguities.

poolAccess.affixFamilyPartitions: Out of scope for this file. naming.v1.json is explicit that family ids are mechanical, not flavour (idNamespaces.affixFamilies). The affix DISPLAY words in ssot-affixes.md §4.12's word table are a separate, already-shipped table with its own word_plant override column; this registry does not restate or replace it.

kindsExemptFromPools._note: Not every kind draws its names from a reserved pool, and pretending otherwise blocks content for no benefit. A gem partition reported BLOCKED because no gem pools exist — correctly, given the rule as written. But gems should not have pools: their naming is deliberately SYSTEMATIC (element x form: Ember Shard, Frost Crystal), which is what makes twenty inserts scannable in an inventory. A disjoint word pool would fight that system rather than support it. The pools exist to stop sixty base-type partitions sounding alike; a kind whose whole readability comes from sounding alike is the exception that proves it.

exempt.reason: systematic element x form naming; readability comes from the pattern, not from variety.
exempt.stillApplies: global name and nameKey collision checks, the naming patterns, and every tag/element/registry rule.

exempt.reason: authors template strings, not item names.
authors numeric points under named ids.
authors verbs and cost shapes, not named objects.
ten of its ids ship already and are consumed by live code; the vocabulary is fixed, not drawn.

kindsExemptFromPools.note: Every other kind — base-type, unique, set, charm, socket-word, consumable, enhancement-milestone, affix-family display names — draws from the pools.

nounPools._note: Keyed '{roleId}.{frame}'. 32 pools, one per role-frame in core.v1.json plus the commander-only standard on both frames. These are head-nouns: what the thing IS. Frame-true by construction - a rooted, handless plant frame gets no oven mitt and no wheelbarrow, and the humanoid frame gets no calyx. The humanoid side is scavenged rather than forged: what a body in this world actually straps on is a traffic pylon, a bucket, a screen shutter, a football shin pad, a pool flipper. See v2Note.

classRungAdjectivePools._note: Keyed '{ladder}.{frame}.{rungId}', matching classes.v1.json's classLadders exactly. 24 pools. These carry material and weight, never flavour - that is the theme pools' job, and keeping the two apart is what lets an author combine one of each without the normalizer seeing a repeat. On the humanoid frame the material is scavenged: cloth is second-hand and hemmed, plate is galvanised sheet and solder, scale is corrugated and tiled, and the seal rung is paperwork rather than oaths.

themeAdjectivePools._note: Keyed themeId, 13 pools, matching themes.v1.json after the wave-0 cut (field-manual removed, permafrost-seed merged into frostbitten-vanguard). Neither removed id appears anywhere in this file. Each pool was written against its theme's `identity` and `avoid` lists, so the adjectives carry the theme's separations too: rot-bloom is cyclical and ecological where charnel-bloom is battlefield-specific; hollow-orchard is a quiet place where sunwoven-almanac is a body of knowledge.

conceptPools._note: Keyed themeId, 13 pools. These fill the Concept slot of naming.v1.json's of-construct pattern. Single tokens: 'of the Turning', 'of Rusted Oxide'. A two-word concept is the author pairing a concept with a theme adjective or a noun - 'of the Charnel Bloom' is conceptPools.charnel-bloom.charnel plus nounPools['head-guard.plant'].bloom, and both halves resolve.

uniqueSetSeedPools._note: Keyed themeId, 13 pools. Proper-noun-flavoured material for the 20 unique and 5 set partitions - words that sound named rather than assembled. Each is atomic: registered whole, resolved whole, never decomposed (see entryShape.resolutionOrder). A seed can be a whole name on its own ('Thornmantle'), the Base of an of-construct ('Mulchmother of the Turning'), or one half of a compound. It is a starting point, not a finished name - an author that ships all 10 verbatim has not done the job.

selfCheck.surfaceFormUniqueness: verified - every one of the 1593 surface forms maps to exactly one canonical id
selfCheck.nearDuplicateStems: verified for the v2 rewrite - the humanoid pools introduce no new stem pair, and dropping `padded` from armour.humanoid.cloth also cleared its overlap with `pad` in manipulator.plant. Four pairs remain, all inside pools v2 did not touch: awn/awning, bud/budding, burr/buried, sod/sodden.
selfCheck.connectiveLeakage: verified - none of of/the/a/and appears as a canonical id or a surface form
selfCheck.floors: verified - every pool meets its perPoolMinimums floor
selfCheck.waveNote: standard.humanoid and standard.plant added during wave 0b review. core.v1.json carries 16 roles including the commander-only standard; the original F1 brief said 30 role-frame pools, so the banner role had no vocabulary at all. Collision-checked against every pre-existing canonical id and surface form before insertion (one clash, pennant, was found and replaced with labarum).
selfCheck.v2Recount: Recounted after the v2 humanoid rewrite. idsPerPool now lists every pool including standard.humanoid and standard.plant, which v1's table omitted, so the per-pool numbers add up to poolCount for the first time.
selfCheck.shapeDefectStandardPlant: FIXED. standard.plant now uses the slot-keyed entryShape ({noun:[...]}) with single-token surface forms, matching standard.humanoid. The multi-token forms it previously carried ("Taproot Idol", "Bloom Staff") could never resolve: the normalizer tokenizes on whitespace, so a two-word surface form splits into two tokens neither of which is registered. Single-token compounds match the humanoid pool convention (Windsock, Yardsign, Whirligig). Collision-checked against every id and form outside this pool.
selfCheck.standardRungAdjectives: Added wave 0c after re-pilot R3 reported BLOCKED. classes.v1.json v2 introduced the commander standard class ladder (field-standard/ceremonial-standard, withy-totem/heartwood-totem) but no matching classRungAdjectivePools existed, so the compound naming pattern <Adjective> <Base> had no adjective source and the partition was literally unauthorable. The agent stopped and said so rather than inventing vocabulary, which is exactly the contract behaviour.

hardestToFill.why: The two humanoid pools with no domestic vocabulary waiting for them. A scavenged world has plenty of words for what you hold and what you wear, and almost none for what sits on a shoulder - so ward-array went to the parts of a car and a roof that already bolt onto an edge (fender, bumper, cowl, spoiler, downspout, batten, girder, rollbar), which reads as strapped-on protection without borrowing a single pauldron. jewel-minor-b is worse: a suburb has one ring per hand at most and no second one at all. Rather than invent jewellery, the second binding became the paperwork that binds you in this world - receipt, coupon, licence, warranty, deed. It reads as a slot, it is funny in the right register, and it shares nothing with jewel-minor-a's hardware drawer (washer, grommet, gasket, ferrule, shim, nut).

Four adjacent heavy rungs across two ladders that all want the same twelve English words: dense, hard, massive, rigid, thick, solid. The near-duplicate stem check kept rejecting pairs the exact check allowed (weighted/weighty, hammer/hammered, knot/knotted). Resolved by splitting the sense of 'heavy' per ladder: plate is sheet metal and fasteners (galvanised, soldered, bevelled, industrial), blunt is kinetic (bludgeoning, jarring, bruising), bark is surface texture (corky, scabrous, lichened), heartwood is age and density (petrified, timeworn, immemorial, inert). Each rung now describes a different reason for being heavy.

openAmbiguities: Charm partitions have no theme exclusivity. naming.v1.json splits charms by power axis (off-ctrl / surv-util / econ) and this file's theme pools are keyed by themeId, so three charm agents share read access to all 13 themes with nothing but the corpus-wide normalizer between them. Either the fleet plan re-partitions charms by theme, or a reviewer accepts that ~60 charm names are the one place in wave 1 where thematic spread is monitored rather than structurally guaranteed. Not a decision this file makes.

Hybrid frame has no noun pools. core.v1.json's third frame carries 13 of the 15 roles and takes a base type from either pure frame's ladder, so it needs no vocabulary of its own today. If hybrid ever gets its own base types rather than borrowing, it needs 13 more noun pools and they must be disjoint from both pure frames - which, given verdant-graft is precisely the theme about that body, is a v2 conversation and not a small one.

The commander-only `standard` role (banner / root-totem) has no noun pool, matching naming.v1.json's decision not to pre-allocate it an id prefix. If it is authored later it needs a 31st and 32nd noun pool.

Affix display words (ssot-affixes.md §4.12's word table, including its word_plant per-frame override column) are deliberately not restated here. They are an existing shipped table; duplicating them into this registry would create exactly the two-ids-one-idea situation the whole file exists to prevent. Whoever runs the affix partitions should confirm that table is still the source of truth before wave 1a starts.

Per-frame flavour overrides. naming.v1.json's perFrameNaming notes that some words differ by frame (a band-C family reads 'Quickening' on humanoid, 'Blooming' on plant). This file handles frame at the noun and class-rung level, where frame is structural, but theme adjectives and concepts are frame-neutral. If a theme word turns out to need a plant override, it should be added as an extra surface form on the SAME canonical id, never as a second entry.
frozenNote: FROZEN v2. Consumed by the wave-1 authoring fleet. No in-place edit from here: a required change is registryVersion 3 plus an explicit decision on which partitions re-run. A silently edited registry splits the corpus into pre-edit and post-edit semantics that nothing downstream can tell apart.
minCompatibleNote: v2 REVOICED all 16 humanoid noun pools and 10 humanoid adjective pools — a v1-authored humanoid partition drew from a medieval arsenal that no longer exists, so it must re-run. v3 fixed the standard.plant entry shape and v4 added the commander class-rung adjectives; both additive.
stage1aFrozen: Stage 1a authored and validated at 0 errors (205 entries, 25 files). From here a change to this registry invalidates authored content unless minCompatibleVersion says otherwise.
